title: Sumo Wrestling with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D sumo wrestling game using Three.js with a full undo/redo system. Generate a single HTML file with everything inline.

## Scene Setup
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 12, 18) looking at the origin.
- Lights: AmbientLight (0xffffff, 0.4) and DirectionalLight (0xffffff, 0.8) at (5, 10, 5).
- Ground: A circular ring (dohyo) of radius 5 units, rendered as a flat cylinder (radius 5, height 0.2) colored sandy tan (0xd2b48c) centered at origin. Add a white torus ring (inner radius 4.8, tube 0.05) on the surface to mark the boundary.
- Player 1 (red): A capsule-like sumo wrestler made from a sphere (radius 0.7) on top of a cylinder (radius 0.6, height 0.8), colored 0xcc3333, starting at position (-2, 0.6, 0).
- Player 2 (blue): Same shape, colored 0x3333cc, starting at position (2, 0.6, 0).
- Each wrestler has a mass property: player1.mass = 1.0, player2.mass = 1.0.

## Physics & Game Logic
- The game is turn-based. Each turn, the active player charges in a direction and moves.
- Movement: When the active player charges, they move 1.0 units in the chosen direction. If they collide with the opponent (distance between centers < 1.4), the opponent is pushed away by 1.5 units in the same direction.
- A wrestler is eliminated (ring-out) if their distance from origin exceeds 5.0 units after any move.
- Friction: after each move, both wrestlers slide 0.1 units toward the center (simulating footing recovery), but only if they are inside the ring.
- Turns alternate: Player 1 goes first (turn 1), then Player 2 (turn 2), etc.

## Controls
- Arrow keys (Up/Down/Left/Right) set the charge direction for the current player.
- Spacebar executes the charge (applies the move for the current turn).
- 'Z' key triggers Undo (reverts to previous game state).
- 'Y' key triggers Redo (re-applies an undone move).
- 'R' key resets the entire game.

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain a history stack of game states. Each state snapshot includes: both player positions (x, z), current turn number, active player, scores, and game-over status.
- After each move (spacebar), push the new state onto the history stack and clear the redo stack.
- Undo pops the current state and pushes it onto the redo stack, restoring the previous state.
- Redo pops from the redo stack and pushes onto the history stack.
- Maximum history depth: 50 states.

## Scoring
- When a wrestler is pushed out of the ring, the other player scores 1 point. After scoring, both wrestlers reset to starting positions and a new round begins. First to 3 points wins.

## HUD (DOM overlay)
- Top-left: 'Player 1 Score: X' in red text.
- Top-right: 'Player 2 Score: X' in blue text.
- Top-center: 'Turn: N | Active: Player X' and below it 'Direction: [arrow]'.
- Bottom-center: 'History: N states | Redo: M states' showing stack sizes.
- When game ends, display 'Player X Wins!' in large centered gold text.
- Add small instruction text at the bottom.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- `player1X`, `player1Z`: Player 1 position (numbers, 2 decimal places).
- `player2X`, `player2Z`: Player 2 position (numbers, 2 decimal places).
- `player1Score`, `player2Score`: integer scores.
- `turnNumber`: integer starting at 1.
- `activePlayer`: 1 or 2.
- `direction`: string 'up'|'down'|'left'|'right'|'none'.
- `historySize`: integer count of history stack.
- `redoSize`: integer count of redo stack.
- `gameOver`: boolean.
- `winner`: 0 (no winner), 1, or 2.
- `lastAction`: string describing last action ('charge', 'undo', 'redo', 'reset', 'none').
- `player1InRing`: boolean (distance from origin <= 5.0).
- `player2InRing`: boolean.
- `distanceBetween`: number, distance between the two players.

Update window.__3D_STATE__ after every state change. Ensure all numeric values are never NaN.
physics_constraints: Turn-based movement: 1.0 unit per charge. Collision threshold: 1.4 units between centers. Push distance: 1.5 units. Ring-out at distance > 5.0 from origin. Friction: 0.1 unit pull toward center after each move. Positions must remain NaN-free. Undo/redo must perfectly restore all state values.
